title: Low-weight Pauli dynamics and truncation error
abstract: Derives a normalized Pauli 2-norm truncation-error bound for concrete circuits of disjoint-support Hermitian Pauli rotations, with explicit locality, angle, step-count, and cutoff hypotheses. Develops a faithful matrix representation, Pauli coefficient reconstruction, finite Schur bounds, and reusable scalar multi-jump ladder estimates. Also proves a combinatorial light-cone bound and exact counterexamples showing why repeated product-formula layers must count toward the layer exponent. This is the norm-level analysis, not a formalization of expectation-value accuracy, Hamiltonian approximation, or the paper's full algorithm.

informal.Lean4LPD.PauliString.pauliNorm_layerStep: For an observable supported on Pauli weights at most ko, a block of Γ positive-many disjoint-support layers of Hermitian rotations of weight at most kh, kh ≥ 2, and |sin θ| ≤ a ≤ αt/r with α > 0 and t ≥ 0, truncation to weight ko + m(kh - 1) after each of r blocks has Pauli 2-norm error at most (2Γ(kh - 1)αt)^(m+1) (e(m+1))^(ko/(kh-1)) times the input norm. The conditions include m ≥ 1, r ≥ 5, m ≤ r, rΓ ≥ 8(m+1)^2, and r ≥ 8e^2(ko+kh-1)αt. Γ counts every layer of the actual block, including repeated product-formula layers.
informal.Lean4LPD.l2_opNorm_le_schur: A finite rectangular matrix over any RCLike field, with absolute row sums bounded by nonnegative R and absolute column sums bounded by nonnegative C, has Euclidean operator norm at most sqrt(RC).
informal.Lean4LPD.PauliString.reachable_weight_le: Every Pauli string reachable through a list of disjoint-support kh-local layers, kh ≥ 1, has weight at most its initial weight times kh raised to the number of layers. Reachability is combinatorial; this theorem does not assert that a reachable coefficient is nonzero.
informal.Lean4LPD.LayerCounterexample.actual_disc: For the explicit eight-qubit second-order word L1,L2,L2,L1 and angles 0 < θ < π/2, truncating the evolved weight-one input at weight one discards a nonzero coefficient of weight greater than four. Thus the two distinct layer types give an invalid bound 1*2^2; repetitions must be counted.
